name: Will pool fill-in reduce home value or help resale?

mainEntity.name: Does filling in a pool usually hurt resale value, help resale, or depend on the neighborhood?
mainEntity.text: Does filling in a pool usually hurt resale value, help resale, or depend on the neighborhood?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether pool fill-in helps resale depends on the local market and the type of buyer the home attracts. In some neighborhoods, a worn-out pool can be a liability because buyers worry about maintenance, safety, and repair costs. Removing it can make the property feel larger, more usable, and easier to maintain. In other areas, especially where pools are a strong lifestyle feature, eliminating a usable pool may reduce appeal. The decision should factor in lot size, privacy, climate, neighborhood expectations, and the condition of the existing pool. Homeowners planning to sell soon should talk to a local real estate professional and compare the cost of keeping, repairing, or removing the pool. A well-executed fill-in can improve marketability if it creates a cleaner, more functional yard and avoids visible settlement or drainage problems.
acceptedAnswer.description: Pool fill-in can help or hurt resale depending on the neighborhood, lot size, buyer profile, and condition of the pool itself. In some markets, removing an unused or expensive-to-maintain pool makes the property more attractive. In others, buyers may prefer to keep a functional pool.
